subject: Model issues- is there a better way to build this model?

messages.author: 778746842555fe22
messages.subject: Model issues- is there a better way to build this model?
parts:
Hi All,

I'm trying to fit a model in Rstan that is a 2D elliptical exponential distribution (typical for a disk galaxy) convolved with a 2D normal (similar to the atmospheric point spread function). If you're curious, this is with a slightly longer term goal of using Stan to fit intrinsic galaxy profiles to real images, but for now I'm just playing with toy sampled data.

I can generate a 3 mixture model with:

library(hyper.fit) #can get from install_github('asgr/hyper.fit'), used for rotdata2d
library(sphereplot) #on CRAN, used for sph2car
library(mvtnorm) #on CRAN, used for rmvnorm for the PSF

theta=c(30,70,110)
shape=c(2,4,6)
xcen=c(0,-5,5)
ycen=c(0,5,-3)
axrat=c(0.1,0.5,0.7)
N=c(1e2,1e2,1e2)
tempM2xyrot={}
for(i in 1:length(theta)){
  tempM2=rexp(N[i],shape[i])
  tempM2xy=sph2car(runif(N[i],0,360),lat=0,radius=sqrt(tempM2))[,1:2]
  tempM2xy[,2]=tempM2xy[,2]*axrat[i]
  rottemp=rotdata2d(tempM2xy[,1],tempM2xy[,2],theta[i])
  tempM2xyrot=rbind(tempM2xyrot,cbind(rottemp[,1]+xcen[i],rottemp[,2]+ycen[i]))
}
#Here I add the PSF convolution/smoothing to the intrinsic galaxy data
PSF=rmvnorm(sum(N),mean=c(0,0),sigma = matrix(c(0.01,0,0,0.01),ncol=2))
tempM2list=list(x=tempM2xyrot[,1]+PSF[,1], y=tempM2xyrot[,2]+PSF[,2], N=length(tempM2xyrot[,1]), J=length(theta), PSFsig=0.01)

This makes the following plot, where three well separated mixture components are clearly visible and you can see their axial ratio and rotation (parameters we fit for):



My model to fit the 2D exponentials and the convolving 2D normal PSF is done with latent variables (which I think is the correct way to approach the problem).

multexpoxy.stan <- "
//utility deprojection functions
functions {
  real deprojr( real x, real y, real theta, real axrat){
    real xprime;
    real yprime;
    real thetarad;
    thetarad <- -theta*pi()/180;
    xprime <- (cos(thetarad)*x-sin(thetarad)*y);
    yprime <- (sin(thetarad)*x+cos(thetarad)*y)/axrat;
    return sqrt(pow(xprime,2)+pow(yprime,2));
  }
  real deprojr2( real x, real y, real theta, real axrat){
    real xprime;
    real yprime;
    real thetarad;
    thetarad <- -theta*pi()/180;
    xprime <- (cos(thetarad)*x-sin(thetarad)*y);
    yprime <- (sin(thetarad)*x+cos(thetarad)*y)/axrat;
    return pow(xprime,2)+pow(yprime,2);
  }
}
data {
  int J;
  int N;
  real x[N];
  real y[N];
  real PSFsig;
}
parameters {
  real<lower=-20,upper=20> xcen[J];
  real<lower=-20,upper=20> ycen[J];
  real<lower=0,upper=10> shape[J];
  real<lower=-270,upper=270> theta[J];
  real<lower=0,upper=1> axrat[J];
  real<lower=-20,upper=20> xtrue[N];
  real<lower=-20,upper=20> ytrue[N];
}
model {
  vector [N] prob;
  real PSF;
  real rdeproj;
  real xprime;
  real yprime;
  for(i in 1:N){
    prob[i] <- 0;
  }
  xcen ~ uniform(-20,20);
  ycen ~ uniform(-20,20);
  shape ~ uniform(0, 10);
  theta ~ uniform(-270, 270);
  axrat ~ uniform(0, 1);
  xtrue ~ uniform(-20,20);
  ytrue ~ uniform(-20,20);
  for(j in 1:J){
    for (i in 1:N){
      rdeproj <- deprojr2(xtrue[i]-xcen[j],ytrue[i]-ycen[j],theta[j],axrat[j]);
      prob[i] <- prob[i] + shape[j]*exp(-rdeproj*shape[j])/axrat[j];
    }
  }
  for(i in 1:N){
    xprime <- xtrue[i]-x[i];
    yprime <- ytrue[i]-y[i];
    PSF <- sqrt(pow(xprime,2)+pow(yprime,2));
    increment_log_prob(normal_log(PSF,0,0.01));
  }
  increment_log_prob(sum(log(prob)));
}
"

However even starting the model at the correct solution things go badly (here I use optimizing, but I get a the same issue when running stan, which maybe hints it's something more basic than a complex sampling/initialisation issue):

> tempoptim=optimizing(object=stan_model(model_code=multexpoxy.stan),data=tempM2list,init=list(xcen=c(0,-5,5),ycen=c(0,5,-3),shape=c(2,4,6),theta=c(30,70,110),axrat=c(0.1,0.5,0.7),xtrue=tempM2list$x,ytrue=tempM2list$y))
Error: Rejecting initial value:
  Gradient evaluated at the initial value is not finite.
  Stan can't start sampling from this initial value.

When I remove the PSF part (both in the data generation and in the second loop over N in the model) and change things back to x and y (measured) rather than xtrue and ytrue (latent) things work nicely, and I can recover the inputs. I think I'm doing something basic wrong, but I can't quite unpick it. Any suggestions would be appreciated.

Thanks,

Aaron

messages.subject: Re: Model issues- is there a better way to build this model?
parts: Looks like I've answered my own question. I needed to use the the multivariate normal, not to transform x and y into a radius and use the normal. I knew the former was the better way to do this, but I assumed the latter should work approximately well to. Seems this is where something in Stan wasn't happy and things become non-linear.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Model issues- is there a better way to build this model?
parts:
Thanks for the follow up. The original question was too tough for
me, but I thought Michael might be tempted ...

We recommend against uniform priors on closed intervals unless
the intervals arise from a "physical" constraint (in the way that (0,1) is a
constraint for bernoulli or binomial parameters). Instead of
uniform(-20, 20), assuming you expect values up to 20, would be to
have normal(0, 10) on an unconstrained parameter.

- Bob
